Alignment.description:
A line on the ground: the path vehicles take, in travel order.
Purely geographic — it carries no timing and no stops, and
materialization only uses it for drawing, never for scheduling.
Patterns run one by reference ([`Pattern::alignment`]); any number
may share one, and one no pattern runs still stands.

AlignmentPoint.description:
One point of an [`Alignment`], with the distance along it where
one was published (in the units of the pattern stops' distances).
Its fields are declared in canonical key order (RFC 8785, D-169), so
its canonical bytes stream in one pass.

Anchor.description:
Where a service day's second zero sits. `NoonMinusTwelve` is the
GTFS convention, adopted on its merits rather than for
compatibility: no DST transition occurs near noon, so offsets
stay unambiguous on change days. The authored model makes the
convention *explicit* where GTFS leaves it to inference.

oneOf.description: Seconds after "noon minus 12h" of the service date.

Area.description: A fare area: a set of stops.

Attribution.description: An organization credited for the data.

AttributionScope.description:
What an attribution credits: the whole dataset (`None` on the
attribution), or one operator, route, or trip.

Block.description:
One vehicle's work: trips in order with the layovers between
them. Authored (runcutting), not derived from trip rows. A block
may hold trips of service types that never share a day; on each
day it is the trips running that day, in this order.

BookingKind.description: How far ahead a ride must be booked.

oneOf.description: Booked any time up to the ride.
Booked the same day, some minutes ahead.
Booked one or more days ahead.

BookingRule.description: How riders book a demand-responsive ride.

booking_days.description: The service type whose days count as booking days.

last_day.description:
Prior days: the last day (days before the ride) and time a
booking is taken, and the first.

notice_min_minutes.description: Same day: the minimum and maximum minutes of notice.

CalendarRule.description:
Which days a service type runs on, as authored rules rather than
GTFS exception rows: weekday flags plus date ranges, with explicit
per-date exceptions that always win.

exceptions.description: Explicit per-date overrides; always beat the weekly rule.

ranges.description:
Inclusive date ranges; a date in any range with its weekday
flagged runs.

Contactless.description: Whether contactless bank cards are accepted.

Coord.description:
A WGS84 position. Authored geometry (a pattern's alignment) is
model data — `lat` first, matching `Stop`'s field order. (GeoJSON
views at the boundary reorder to [lon, lat]; the model never
stores GeoJSON order.)

oneOf.description: Service runs this date even though the weekly rule says no.

Service does not run this date even though the weekly rule
says yes.

trips.description:
The demand-responsive trips, by id (trip ids are unique across
these and the network's scheduled trips).

zones.description:
The zones riders are picked up or dropped off in: a GeoJSON
FeatureCollection whose features' ids are the zone ids.

DemandTrip.description:
A demand-responsive trip: a route's service under a service type,
visiting places in order.

Departs.description: When a trip departs: once, or as a frequency.

oneOf.description: One instance, starting at `start_secs`.

A frequency trip: one instance at `start_secs + k * headway_secs`
while the start is `< end_secs`, per band (end-exclusive), all
sharing the trip's id and times. `exact`: the instances run on
exactly that grid (otherwise riders are promised the headway,
not the minutes).

Direction.description: One direction of a route, as a planner names it.

DurationLimit.description: How the time limit of a fare transfer is measured.

FareLegJoinRule.description: Two consecutive legs that fares count as one.

FareLegRule.description:
Which product a leg costs: by network, areas, and timeframes
(unset: any), the most specific (highest priority) rule winning.

FareMediaKind.description: What a fare is held on.

oneOf.description: Nothing: cash or a fare paid with no medium.
Contactless bank card or device.

FareOffer.description:
One way a fare product is sold: its price for a rider category on
a medium (unset: any).

FareTransferKind.description: What a transfer between legs costs.

oneOf.description: The first leg's fare plus the transfer's.
Every leg's fare plus the transfer's.
The transfer's fare alone.

FareTransferRule.description: What changing from one leg group to another costs.

networks.description: Groups of routes fares treat alike (a route names its own).

products.description:
What riders buy, by id — one offer per rider category and
medium it is sold for.

zone_fare_rules.description: Where each zone fare applies, in published order.

Layover.description: Recovery time between two trips of a block.

after_trip.description: Index into the block's trips: the layover follows that trip.

at.description: Where the vehicle waits, if it matters.

index.description: Order of the levels: 0 is the ground, negative is below it.

LocationGroup.description: Stops served as one: a rider may board or alight at any of them.

Mode.description: Vehicle modes as a domain concept, not GTFS's numeric codes.

NetworkVersion.description:
The network document's version. A network built in code is the
current version; a document read without one is version 1.

contactless.description: Whether contactless bank cards are accepted; `None` = unknown.

timezone.description: The timezone every time of the operator's service is in.

Pathway.description: A way between two places of a station (stops, station parts).

both_ways.description: Walkable both ways (`false`: only from → to).

reversed_signposted_as.description: What the signs say walking it to → from.

signposted_as.description: What the signs say walking it from → to.

oneOf.description: A fare gate: paying happens crossing it.
An exit gate: a fare gate's way out.

Pattern.description:
A route pattern: the stop sequence a planner draws along its
alignment, with the profiles new trips are timed from. Every trip
runs a pattern. A document written before alignments (an inline
`path`) is version 1, refused at its load and brought forward by
the migration (`migrate.rs`), which moves its line.

alignment.description:
The [`Alignment`] the pattern runs, by id. `None` (omitted)
means "draw stop-to-stop lines".

direction.description:
Which of the route's [`Route::directions`] this pattern runs
in; `None` (omitted) when the route has none or the pattern is
not yet placed. Bay and short-turn variants share a direction.

name.description: Human-facing description, e.g. "5-K Ave to Downtown via MLK".

PatternStop.description: One stop visit within a pattern.

continuous_pickup.description:
Continuous stopping from here to the next stop; `None` = the
route's.

distance_m.description: Meters along the pattern from its first stop. Non-decreasing.

distance_published.description:
Whether `distance_m` was published (in the publisher's own
units) rather than estimated; an estimate is never published.

headsign.description:
What the vehicle's sign says at this visit, where it differs
from the trip's headsign (this visit only — `visit_destination`).

pickup_booking.description: The booking rule a rider follows to board (alight) here.

timepoint.description:
An exact stop: every trip of the pattern carries both its
arrival and its departure here. Other stops may leave times
unscheduled (they materialize by distance between scheduled
neighbours).

PatternTrips.description:
One pattern's trips under one service type. Everything RAPTOR and
dispatch consume derives from these. Not a planner's "schedule":
the timetable a planner reads is a route's direction under one
service type, across all its patterns (`listing::timetable`).

PlanMeta.description:
The service-plan frame of a network document. Agencies implement
a few service changes ("picks") a year at defined dates — the
only times permanent stop/route changes are allowed — and each
pick is one of these documents, effective from its service
change date until superseded by the next. A document without
plan metadata is unversioned (e.g. a fresh GTFS import).

effective_from.description:
The service change date this plan takes effect, "YYYY-MM-DD".
None on unversioned documents; a plan in a chain must have one.

id.description:
The plan's identity — the sync key (LWW per plan). Empty on
unversioned documents.

Publisher.description: Who publishes the dataset, and what it covers.

start_date.description: The first and last dates the dataset covers, "YYYYMMDD".

RiderCategory.description: Who a fare is for (adult, senior, youth).

default.description: The category a rider is in unless they say otherwise.

Route.description:
A route as a planner authors it: its public name (the short one
riders see, "12"), its long name ("Lincoln"), a closed mode set.
Display it by [`Route::label`].

contactless.description:
Whether contactless bank cards are accepted on board; `None` =
as the operator says.

continuous_pickup.description:
Riders may board (alight) anywhere along the route's line, by
this rule; `None` = only at stops.

directions.description:
The ways the route runs, by id, each named the way the planner
says it ("To Downtown", "Northbound"). A pattern belongs to at
most one; a timetable is one direction on one service type.
Empty (omitted) for a route nobody has split into directions.

fare_network.description: The fare network it belongs to.

name.description:
The short public name; empty for a route known only by its
long name.

operator.description: Who runs it; `None` = the network's only operator.

sort_order.description: Where the route sorts in lists (lower first).

vehicle_type.description:
The published vehicle type code, where the mode alone does not
say it (an extended type such as a regional rail or night bus).

ServiceType.description:
A service type: the service identifier planners design —
Weekday, Saturday, Sunday, a holiday — linked to the days it
runs by its calendar rule. This, not the day-of-month, is the
axis planners design on (GTFS calls it service_id).

rule.description:
The days it runs: weekday flags plus date ranges, with
explicit per-date exceptions that always win.

StationPart.description:
An entrance, node, or boarding area: part of a station (a boarding
area is part of its platform), linked to the rest by pathways.

at.description: Where it is, when published (required of an entrance).

parent.description: The station (or, for a boarding area, the platform) it is part of.

StationPartKind.description: A part of a station riders walk through but never board at.

oneOf.description: A point where pathways meet.
Where on a platform a rider boards.

Stop.description:
A stop as a planner authors it: one name, one location, optional
parent (platform-in-station groupings) — a stop riders board at,
or a station grouping stops.

transfer.description:
A designated transfer point: where the network intends riders
to change vehicles. Authored intent, not a badge — the flag
only means something composed with the routes that meet there
(validation requires at least two; the analysis ops measure
the timed connections it enables).

StopInfo.description:
What a rider can know about a place beyond its name and point.
Shared by stops and station parts.

code.description: The short code riders see on the sign or type into a phone.

fare_zone.description: The fare zone the place is in (zone fares).

spoken_name.description: How the name is read aloud, where it differs from the text.

street_access.description:
A station's stop: reached straight from the street (`true`) or
only through the station (`false`).

timezone.description: The place's own timezone, where it differs from its operator's.

wheelchair.description:
Whether a wheelchair user can board here (or, for an entrance,
get in); `None` = unknown (a child place inherits its parent's).

StopKind.description:
What kind of place a [`crate::Stop`] is: a stop or platform riders
board at, or a station grouping them.

StopOffset.description:
A trip's time at one pattern stop: seconds after the instance's
start. `None` = not scheduled there (the stop materializes between
its scheduled neighbours). The first arrival is 0; the first and
last stops, and every timepoint, carry both.

StopRule.description:
Whether, and how, riders may board or alight: at a stop (pickup,
drop-off) or anywhere along the line (continuous stopping).

oneOf.description: The rider phones the agency to arrange it.
The rider arranges it with the driver.

Timeframe.description:
A span of a service type's day fares treat alike (peak, off-peak).
No start and end means the whole day.

TimingProfile.description:
Run-time profile for NEW trips departing in a time band
`[start_secs, end_secs)` — the planner's production tool. Stored
trips carry their own times; a profile never governs them.

`at_timepoints` is cumulative seconds from the first timepoint at
each of the pattern's timepoints, in pattern order (the first
entry is 0).

TransferEnd.description:
One side of a transfer rule: where (and from or onto what) the
rider changes. Unset parts match anything.

TransferKind.description: What a transfer rule says about changing vehicles.

oneOf.description: A recommended place to change.
The departing vehicle waits for the arriving one.
Changing takes at least `min_transfer_secs`.
Changing is not possible here.
The rider stays in the vehicle from one trip to the next.
The rider must leave the vehicle between the two trips.

TransferRule.description: How riders change vehicles between two places, routes, or trips.

Translation.description:
One text of the network in another language. `table` and `field`
name the text the way the published dataset does ("stops",
"stop_name"); the text is found by record (`record`, and
`sub_record` where a record needs two keys) or by its value in the
original language.

Trip.description:
One trip: the agency's id, when it departs, and its own time at
every stop of its pattern (`times[i]` is `pattern.stops[i]`). Its
fields are declared in canonical key order (RFC 8785, D-169), so its
canonical bytes stream in one pass (`cap-abi`, `jcs_law_test.rs`).

short_name.description: The trip's public number, where riders know it by one.

wheelchair.description:
Whether the vehicle takes a wheelchair (bikes, cars); `None` =
unknown.

TripRef.description:
A block's reference to a trip, by id. A block runs a trip whole
(as GTFS has it): a frequency trip in a block is every one of its
instances, back to back.

Visit.description:
One visit of a demand-responsive trip: a place, served at times or
within a window (seconds after the service day's anchor).

timepoint.description:
An exact time (`Some(true)`), an approximate one
(`Some(false)`), or unstated.

window_start_secs.description: The window riders are picked up or dropped off in.

WeekdaySet.description:
Authored weekday flags. A rule with no flags still runs on dates
explicitly `Added` (special-event service) — see `runs_on`.

ZoneFare.description: A zone fare: its price and how it may be used.

transfer_secs.description: How long transfers (or the fare) stay valid.

ZoneFareRule.description:
Where a zone fare applies: on a route, from a zone to a zone, or
through a zone. Unset parts match anything.

description:
The authored network document. BTreeMap-keyed so serialization is
canonical and per-entity sync falls out later.

alignments.description: The lines on the ground patterns run, by id.

anchor.description:
The service-day time anchor every offset in the network is
measured from. Defaults to the noon-minus-12h convention.

operators.description: Who runs the service, by id.

pattern_trips.description: Every pattern's trips, grouped by (pattern, service type).

plan.description:
The service plan this document is: the versioning frame for
service changes. Defaults to unversioned.

schema_version.description:
The document's version (D-62): written on every write; a
document without one is version 1 (`version.rs`).

service_types.description: The service types: what planners design and link to days.

station_parts.description:
Entrances, nodes, and boarding areas, by id (ids are unique
across these and the stops).

title: Network
